opinion.headline: Indians can afford more food. Why are they still eating poorly?
opinion.hook: Indians are eating poorly despite earning more.
opinion.summary: Low-quality cereals fill plates, while proteins, vegetables, and fruits are lacking. This affects both the poor and the rich. Even affluent urban dwellers consume unhealthy processed foods. India faces a double burden of malnutrition. Better diets require strong policies and nudges. Shifting production incentives to nutritious foods is crucial.
